### Observed differences

- Routing out of A25 changed completely. Earlier, A25's outgoing transitions went to A35 (about 38 in 100), A36 (about 31) and A41 (about 27); in the later window about 96 in 100 go to A27. A25 and A27 were about four event positions apart in roughly 92 in 100 cases earlier, and are immediately consecutive in about 97 in 100 later cases. [DIR005, LAG002]
- Routing out of A26 changed in the matching direction. Earlier, A26 was followed directly by A30 in about 99 in 100 cases (immediately consecutive in about 98 in 100); in the later window A26 leads to A35 (about 35 in 100), A36 (about 32) and A41 (about 31), while A30 now follows about four positions later (about 91 in 100) instead of immediately. [DIR006, LAG005]
- The successors of A35, A36 and A41 shifted accordingly: earlier, each led to A27 in roughly 29–36% of its outgoing transitions; in the later window A27 is almost no longer their successor (about 1 in 100) and A30 appears at about 30–34%. Consistently, A35, A36 and A41 now sit later in the trace (mean position about 0.40 to about 0.58), A27 sits earlier (about 0.46 to about 0.39) and A26 slightly earlier (about 0.60 to about 0.53); all these activities occur in every trace in both windows. [DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- A02 became far less frequent and lost its place on the late path: it appeared in about 75 in 100 traces earlier versus about 21 in 100 later (mean occurrences per trace 0.81 to 0.23). Earlier, about 91% of A02's outgoing transitions went to A50; later only about 13%, spread over many activities. A49 now leads directly to A50 (about 83 in 100, mostly immediately consecutive, versus about 27 in 100 earlier) where it earlier led to A02 (about 72 in 100); A02's mean position moved from about 0.93 (near the trace end) to about 0.55, and the direct A02→A50 adjacency fell from about 99 to about 43 in 100 (the later figure rests on only 14 traces). [OCC001, DIR001, DIR011, LAG009, LAG001, POS001]
- A06 and A10 occur in more traces: participation rose from about 7 to about 19 in 100 (A06) and from about 9 to about 22 in 100 (A10), and both appear as new low-share successors of A14, A47, A49, A36 and A41. The earlier shares rest on only 13 and 17 traces, so the size of this shift is uncertain. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, DIR010, DIR011]
- Some flagged relations were essentially stable: routing from A14 to A15 and from A15 to A16 changed by only about 0.001 on the indicator's own scale. [DIR003, DIR004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a reordering of the mid-process block around A25, A26, A27, A30 and the group A35/A36/A41. Earlier, A25 branched to A35/A36/A41, which led on to A27 about four positions later, while A26 led directly to A30; in the later window A27 immediately follows A25, and A35/A36/A41 run after A26 and lead to A30, which now follows about four positions after A26. This is shown directly by successor replacements and pairwise lags, each backed by about 200 observations per relation in both windows, and the position shifts (A27 earlier, A35/A36/A41 later) agree with it; because every involved activity occurs in all traces in both windows, this is a change in execution order, not in participation. The screening comparison supports treating the pattern as more than chance: 30 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.75 expected for an unchanged process. [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, LAG002, LAG005, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, screening]

Limitations: positions and lags use event positions, so the hypothesis concerns order within the trace, not clock timing; the evidence does not reveal every rewired edge beyond the observed adjacencies and five-step lags; and several flagged relational items were not used because they rest on 1–4 observations in one window (for example A25→A36, A25→A41, A26→A36, A36→A30). [LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008]

Other differences: A02 largely dropped out of the late path — the earlier sequence A49 → A02 → A50 appears replaced by A49 → A50 directly, with A02's trace participation falling from about 75 to about 21 in 100 — and A06 and A10 became more frequent, though from low bases; these are not part of the main hypothesis. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR011, LAG009, OCC002, OCC003]

An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that this reordering is one facet of a single larger restructure that also produced the A02 bypass and the growth of A06 and A10; the two windows show the combined result but cannot establish how these changes connect. [OCC001, DIR011, OCC002, OCC003]
